items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: with a drummer named Ray Churchman. We had been up all night before, hanging out.

ctx.x: I mean April – is an infant. But let me back up – yeah, because it’s coming later. Basically, that takes us up through 1959, ’60. But let me back up to something that really turns out to have a major impact on my life. In 1953, coming back from Lake Hamilton when we played up there, I’m coming back

with a drummer named Ray Churchman. We had been up all night before, hanging out. We’re coming back, and I’m sleeping in the front seat with no seat belt, because seat belts – you didn’t have seat belts at the time. I’m not sure whether a tractor hit us or another car hit the car, threw me – I don't know – some 25 feet out the front window, through the front window. I was in a coma for a week in a place called – it’s where the Quayles live.
